A 220 V DC machine supplies 20 A at 200 V as a generator. The armature
resistance is 0.2 ohm. If the machine is now operated as a motor at same terminal
voltage and current but with the flux increased by 10%, the ratio of motor speed
to generator speed is
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} &\text{For generator,} \\ E&=V+I_aR_a \\ &= 200+20 \times 0.2\\ &=204 \\ &\text{For motor,} \\ V&=E +I_aR_a \\ E&= 200-20 \times 0.2\\ &= 196\\ \frac{E_1}{E_2} &=\frac{N_1}{N_2} \times \frac{\phi _1}{\phi _2}\\ \frac{204}{196}&= \frac{N_1}{N_2} \times\frac{1}{1.1}\\ \therefore \;\;\frac{N_2}{N_1} &=\frac{196}{204 \times 1.1}\\ &=0.87 \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: electrical-machines
questions.question:
The speed of a 4-pole induction motor is controlled by varying the supply
frequency while maintaining the ratio of supply voltage to supply frequency (V/f) constant. At rated frequency of 50 Hz and rated voltage of 400 V its speed is
1440 rpm. Find the speed at 30 Hz, if the load torque is constant
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} N_{s_1} &=\frac{120f_1}{P} \\ &= \frac{120 \times 50}{4}=1500\; \text{rpm}\\ s_1 &=\frac{N_{s_1}-N_{R_1}}{N_{s_1}} \\ &= \frac{1500-1440}{1500}=0.04\\ \text{as}\;\;\frac{V}{f} &=\text{Constant} \\ \frac{V_1}{f_1}&=\frac{V_2}{f_2} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; V_2&=V_1\left ( \frac{f_2}{f_1} \right ) \\ &= 400 \times \frac{30}{50}=240V \end{aligned}\]

Torque developed in induction motor
\(T=\frac{3}{\omega _s}\frac{V^2R'_2/s}{(R'_2/s)^2 +{X'_2}^2}\)
In stable region, slip is very low, so \(\frac{R'_2}{s} \gt \gt X'_2\)
So, T can be approximated as
\[\begin{aligned} T &=\frac{3}{\omega _s}\frac{V^2R'_2/s}{(R'_2/s)^2} \\ &=\frac{3}{\omega _s} \frac{8V^2}{R'_2} \\ T&\propto \frac{sV^2}{f} \\ \frac{T_1}{T_2}&= \frac{s_1}{s_2}\left ( \frac{V_1}{V_2} \right )^2 \times \frac{f_2}{f_1} \end{aligned}\]
as load torque is constant, \(T_1=T_2\)
\[\begin{aligned} s_2 &=s_1 \left ( \frac{V_1}{V_2} \right )^2 \times \frac{f_2}{f_1}\\ &= 0.04 \times \left ( \frac{400}{240} \right )^2 \times \left ( \frac{30}{50} \right )\\ &= 0.067\\ N_{s2} &=\frac{120f_2}{P} \\ &= \frac{120 \times 30}{4}=900 \; \text{rpm}\\ &\text {Rotor speed,}\\ N_{r2}&=N_{s2(1-s_2)} \\ &= 900(1-0.067)\\ &\approx 840 \; \text{rpm} \end{aligned}\]

rated line to line voltage, \(V_{l-l}=400V\)
Phase to neutral voltage, \(V_{p}=\frac{V_{l-l}}{\sqrt{3}}= \frac{400}{\sqrt{3}}V\)
Synchronous speed at 50 Hz
\[\begin{aligned} N_s &=\frac{120f}{P}=\frac{120 \times 50}{4} \\ &=1500 \;\text{rpm} \\ \omega _s &=\frac{2 \pi N_s}{60}=\frac{2 \pi \times 1500}{50} \\ &= 157.08 \; \text{rad/sec} \\ s&= 1\, \; \text{at starting}\ \\ &\text{Starting torque} \\ T_s&= \frac{3}{\omega _s}\frac{V_P^2r'_2}{(r_1+r'_2)^2+(x_1+x'_2)^2}\\ T_s &= \frac{3}{157.08} \times \frac{(400\sqrt{3})^2 \times 0.5}{(1+0.5)^2+(1.2+1.2)^2}\\ &\approx 63.6 \; N-m \end{aligned}\]

questions.explanation:

Copper loss at 15A
\(P_{cu}=762W\)
Full load current =20A
So, copper loss on full load
\[\begin{aligned} P_{cu,fl} &= (P_{cu}) \left ( \frac{20}{15} \right )^2\\ P_{cu,fl} &= 762 \times \left ( \frac{20}{15} \right )^2=1.354 kW \\ & \text{Total losses,}\\ P-1 +P_{cu,fl} &=1.002+1.354 \\ &= 2.356kW \end{aligned}\]

\(P_0=10kW\)
Input power=Output power +losses
\(=10+2.356=12.356kW\)
\[\begin{aligned} \% \text{efficiency} &=\frac{\text{Output power}}{Input Power}\times 100 \\ &= \frac{10}{12.356}\times 100\approx 81\% \end{aligned}\]

A 3-phase, 400 V, 5 kW, star connected synchronous motor having an internal
reactance of 10 \(\Omega\) is operating at 50% load, unity p.f. Now, the excitation is increased by 1%. What will be the new load in percent, if the power factor is to be kept same? Neglect all losses and consider linear magnetic circuit.
questions.explanation:
\(I_{fl}=\frac{5 \times 10^{3}}{\sqrt{3} \times 400 \times 1}=7.21A\)
For synchronous motor,
\[\begin{aligned} E^2 &=(V \cos \theta -I_aR_a)^2 +(V\sin \theta -I_aX_s)^2 \\ E&= \sqrt{(400/\sqrt{3})^2+(10 \times 3.6)^2}\\ &= 233.729V \end{aligned}\]
If there is 1% increase in \(E_2\), then \(E_2\) becomes,
\[\begin{aligned} E_2 &=233.729 \times 1.01=236V \\ \therefore \;\; I_aX &=\sqrt{E_2^2-V^2} \\ &= \sqrt{(236)^2-(400/\sqrt{3})^2}\\ &= 48.93\\ \therefore \;\; I_a&=4.893A \\ \therefore \;\;\% \;\text{load} &= \frac{4.893}{7.21}=67.86\% \end{aligned}\]

A variable w is related to three other variables x, y, z as w=xy/z. The variables
are measured with meters of accuracy \(\pm\)0.5% reading, \(\pm\)1% of full scale value and \(\pm\)1.5% reading. The actual readings of the three meters are 80, 20 and 50 with 100 being the full scale value for all three. The maximum uncertainty in the measurement of w will be
questions.explanation:
Full scale reading of all three =100
Reading of x =80
Reading of y =20
Reading of z =50
\(\delta x=\pm 0.5\)% of reading \(=\pm \frac{0.5 \times 80}{100}=\pm 0.4\)
\(\delta y=\pm 1\)% of reading \(=\pm \frac{1 \times 100}{100}=\pm 1\)
\(\delta z=\pm 1.5\)% of reading \(=\pm \frac{1.5 \times 50}{100}=\pm 0.75\)

A 200/1 Current transformer (CT) is wound with 200 turns on the secondary
on a toroidal core. When it carries a current of 160 A on the primary, the ratio
and phase errors of the CT are found to be -0.5% and 30 minutes respectively.
If the number of secondary turns is reduced by 1 new ratio-error(%) and phaseerror(
min) will be respectively
questions.explanation:
Nominal ratio \(=k_n=\frac{200}{1}=200\)
Primary current \(=I_P=160A\)
Actual ratio \(= R_1=n_1\left ( 1+\frac{I_e}{I_P} \right )\;\;...(i)\)
\(\% \text{Ratio error}\) \(=\frac{k_n - R_1}{R_1}\times 100\)
\(-0.5=\frac{200-R_1}{R_1} \times 100\)
Actual ratio \(=R_1=201\)
\(n_1=\text{turn ratio}=200\)
\(R_1=200\left ( 1+\frac{I_e}{I_P} \right )\;\;...(ii)\)
when number of secondary is reduced by 1
\[\begin{aligned} N_s &= 199\\ n_2&=199 \\ R_2&=n_2\left ( 1+\frac{I_e}{I_P} \right ) \\ &= 199\left ( 1+\frac{I_e}{I_P} \right )\;\;...(iii) \end{aligned}\]
Dividing equation (ii) and (iii),
\[\begin{aligned} \frac{R_1}{R_2} &=\frac{200}{199} \\ \Rightarrow \;R_2 &= R_1 \times \left ( \frac{200}{199} \right )\\ &=201 \times \frac{200}{199}\approx 200 \\ \% \text{Ratio error} &=\frac{k_n-R_2}{R_2} \times 100\\ &= \frac{200-200}{200}\times 100=0 \end{aligned}\]
Phase angle error \(=\theta =\frac{180}{\pi}\left ( \frac{I_m}{I_P} \right )\)
Reduction of one or two turns of the secondary winding, no doubt, reduces the ration error, but it has no effect on the phase angle error.

questions.question:
A 3-phase fully controlled bridge converter with free wheeling diode is fed from
400 V, 50 Hz AC source and is operating at a firing angle of 60\(^{\circ}\). The load current
is assumed constant at 10 A due to high load inductance. The input displacement
factor (IDF) and the input power factor (IPF) of the converter will be
questions.explanation:
Load current is constant
\(I_0=10A\)
In \(3-\phi\) full converter with free wheeling diode, input displacement factor (IDF) \(= \cos \alpha = \cos 60^{\circ}=0.5\)
RMS value of source current
\(I_s=\sqrt{I_0^2 \times \frac{2 \pi}{3} \times \frac{1}{\pi}}=I_0\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\)
RMS value of \(n^{th}\) harmonic
\(I_{sh}=\frac{4I_0}{\sqrt{2}n \pi}\sin \frac{n \pi}{3}\)
RMS value of fundamental current
\(I_{s1}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\pi}I_0 \sin 60^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\pi}I_0\)
Current distortion factor (CDF)
\(=\frac{I_{s1}}{I_s}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\pi}I_0 \times \left ( \frac{1}{I_0}\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \right )\)
\(=\frac{3}{\pi}=0.955\)
Input power factor \((IPF) =CDF \times IDF = 0.955 \times 0.5\approx 0.478\)

questions.question: A voltage commutation circuit is shown in figure. If the turn-off time of the SCR is 50 \(\mu\)sec and a safety margin of 2 is considered, then what will be the approximate minimum value of capacitor required for proper commutation ?
questions.explanation:
In this type of commutation, athyristor carrying load current is commutated by transferring its load current to another incoming thyristor.
Firing of SCR \(Th_1\) commutates \(Th_2\) and subsequently, firing of SCR \(Th_2\) would turn-off \(Th_1\).
Circuit turn-off time \(t_{c1}\) for \(Th_1\)
\(t_{c1}=R_1C \ln 2\)
and circuit turn-off time \(t_{c2}\) for \(Th_2\)
\(t_{c2}=R_2C \ln 2\)
as \(R_1=R_2=50 \Omega\)
\(t_{c2}=t_{c1}=R_1 C \ln 2\)
Safety margin =2
So, \(R_1C \ln 2=2 t_{c1}\)
\(C=\frac{2 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}}{50 \times \ln 2}=2.88 \mu F\)

A 4 pole, 50 Hz, synchronous generator has 48 slots in which a double layer winding is housed. Each coil has 10 turns and is short pitched by an angle to 36\(^\circ\) electrical. The fundamental flux per pole is 0.025 Wb.

The line-to-line induced emf(in volts), for a three phase star connection is approximately
questions.explanation:
In double layer winding
No. of coil = No. of slots =48
Each coil has 10 turns
Total no. of turns \(=48 \times 10=480\)
\[\begin{aligned} T_{ph} &=\text{No. of turns/phase} \\ &= \frac{480}{3}=160 \end{aligned}\]
Slots/pole/phase \(=m=\frac{48}{4 \times 3}=4\)
\[\begin{aligned} \gamma &= \text{slot angle}\\ &=\frac{180 \times \text{poles}}{\text{slots}} \\ &= \frac{180 \times 4}{48}=15^{\circ}\\ &\text{Distribution factor,}\\ k_d&=\frac{\sin \frac{m\gamma }{2}}{m \sin \frac{\gamma }{2}} \\ &= \frac{\sin \left ( \frac{4 \times 15}{2} \right )}{2 \sin \left ( \frac{15}{2} \right )}\\ &= 0.957\\ & \text{Short-pitching angle,}\\ \alpha &=36^{\circ} \end{aligned}\]
For the \(n^{th}\) harmonic, pitch factor,
\(k_p=\cos \frac{n\alpha }{2}\)
pitch factor due to fundamental component
\[\begin{aligned} k_p&=\cos \frac{\alpha }{2}=\cos 18^{\circ}=0.951 \\ &\text{Winding factor,} \\ k_w&=k_dk_p \\ &=0.957 \times 0.951=0.910 \\ &\text{Induced emf per phase,} \\ E_{ph}&= 4.44 k_w f T_{ph}\phi \\ &=4.44 \times 0.91 \times 50 \times 160 \times 0.025 \\ &\approx 808\\ \Rightarrow \;\; E_{line} &=\sqrt{3} E_{ph}=1400V \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
A generator feeds power to an infinite bus through a double circuit transmission line. A 3-phase fault occurs at the middle point of one of the lines. The infinite bus voltage of the generator is 1.1 pu and the equivalent transfer admittance during fault is 0.8 pu. The 100 MVA generator has an inertia constant of 5 MJ/MVA and it was delivering 1.0 pu power prior of the fault with rotor power angle of 30\(^\circ\). The system frequency is 50 Hz.

The initial accelerating power (in pu) will be
questions.explanation:
Before fault:
Electrical power delivered by the generator \(=P_e=1.0p.u.\)
Mechanical input to the generator \(=P_m\)
At steady state,
\(P_m=P_e=1.0p.u.\)
During Fault:
Initial rotorr angle \(=\delta =30^{\circ}\)
Internal voltage of the generator \(=|E_g|=1.1p.u.\)
Voltage of the bus \(=|V|=1p.u.\)
Equivalent transfer admittance =0.8
Transfer reactance \(=x=\frac{1}{0.8}=1.25\)
\((P_e)_f =\) Electrical power delivered by the generator
\(\text{During fault}=\frac{|E_g||V_t|}{x}\sin \delta\)
\((P_e)_f=\frac{1.1 \times 1}{1.25}\sin 30^{\circ}=0.44p.u.\)
Mechanical input do not change during fault
So, \((P_m)_f=1p.u.\)
Accelerating power
\[\begin{aligned} P_a&= (P_m)_f-(P_e)_f\\ P_a&=1-0.44 \\ &= 0.56p.u. \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
A 300 kVA transformer has 95% efficiency at full load 0.8 pf lagging and 96% efficiency at half load, unity pf.
The iron loss \(\left ( P_{i} \right )\) and copper loss\(\left ( P_{c} \right )\) in kW, under full load operation are
questions.explanation:
Iron loss \(=P_i,\) it does not depends on the load.
Full load copper loass \(=P_{c,fl},\) it depends on the load
\(P_{cu}=x^2 P_{c,fl}\)
where,
\(x=\) Fraction of the full load
Rated kVA = S = 300kVA
\(\eta =\)% efficeincy of a transformer
\[\begin{aligned} \eta &=\frac{xS \cos \phi }{x S\cos \phi + P_i+P_{cu}} \\ &= \frac{xS \cos \phi}{x S\cos \phi + P_i+x^2P_{c,fl}} \end{aligned}\]

\((i)\; \; \eta =95\%,\; x=1,\; \cos \phi =0.8\)
\(0.95=\frac{1 \times 300 \times 0.8}{1 \times 300 \times 0.8+P_i+1^2 P_{c,fl}}\)
\(\Rightarrow \;\;P_i+P_{c,fl}=12.63kW\;\;...(i)\)

\((ii)\; \; \eta =96\%,\; x=0.5,\; \cos \phi =1\)
\(0.96=\frac{0.5 \times 300 \times 1}{0.5 \times 300 \times 1+P_i+(0.5)^2 P_{c,fl}}\)
\(\Rightarrow \;\;P_i+P_{c,fl}=6.25kW\;\;...(ii)\)
Solving equation (i) and (ii), we get
\(P_i=4.12kW\) and \(P_{c,fl}=8.51kW\)

questions.question:
A voltage commutated chopper operating at 1 kHz is used to control the speed of dc as shown in figure. The load current is assumed to be constant at 10 A.

The minimum time in \(\mu\) sec for which the SCR M should be ON is
questions.explanation:
Initially, main thyristor (m) and auxiliary thyristor (A) are off and capacitor is assumed charged to voltage V with upper plate positive. When 'm' is turned on at t=0, source voltage V is applied across load and load current \(I_0\) begins to flow which is assumed to remain constant.
With 'm' ON at t=0, anotheroscillatory circuit consisting of C, m, L and D is formed where the capacitor current is given by
\(i_c=V\sqrt{\frac{C}{L}} \sin \omega _0 t=I_p \sin \omega _0 t\)

When, \(\omega _0 t=\pi, i_c=0\)
Between \(0 \\lt t \\lt \frac{\pi}{\omega _0}, i_{T1}=I_0+I_P \sin \omega _0 t\) capacitor voltage charges from \(+V_s \; to \; -V_s\) sinusoidally and the lower plate becomes positive.
At \(\omega _0 t=\pi, i_c=0, i_{T1}=I_0 \text{ and }V_c=-V_s\)
At \(t_1\), thyristor A is turned on and capacitor voltage V applies a reverse voltage across thyristor in and SCR 'm' is turned off. The load current is now carried by C and SCR A.
So, minimum time for which SCR 'm' should be ON.
\[\begin{aligned} T_{min}&=\frac{\pi}{\omega _0}=\pi\sqrt{LC} \\ &= \pi\sqrt{2 \times 10^{-3} \times 1 \times 10^{-6}}=140\mu s \end{aligned}\]
